Districts ask the same three questions before they approve a tool, so this page answers them in that order: what we collect about a student, who else touches it, and how you get it deleted.

It is written to be handed to an IT reviewer rather than read for reassurance, so it names vendors instead of describing them in general terms. If your review needs something this page does not cover, ask and we will answer it in writing.
A student account is a name and a PIN
A student never gives us an email address. There is no field for one anywhere in the student sign-in, and there is no column for one in the students table.

A teacher creates a class, the class gets a code like CSA-7QX4, and a student joins with a display name their teacher will recognize and a four digit PIN. Most teachers use a first name and a last initial. The PIN is stored as a bcrypt hash, so we cannot read it back and neither can anyone who obtains the database
column2: a forgotten PIN is reset by the teacher, never recovered. That is the entire account.

column1: Students who work without a teacher get an ME- code under the same model. Still a display name, still a PIN, still no email.

Our mailing list is a separate thing and it is not connected to any of this. Anyone can subscribe from the footer of the site, and some students do. A subscription creates a marketing contact holding an email address and nothing else: it is not a student account, it does not appear in any class, and it is not linked to a name, a PIN, or a single score. Unsubscribe is in every email we send.

• Email addresses for students. No field, no column.
  • Passwords. A four digit PIN is not a password and we do not ask for one.
  • Date of birth, address, phone number, photograph, or any demographic field.
  • Free typed text, with one exception named above. Quiz answers are stored as option numbers, so a student cannot type something into our database.
  • Location beyond what any web server sees from a request.
  • Anything from a student's device: no camera, no microphone, no browser history, no proctoring, no keystroke logging, no screen capture.

Advertising and analytics on our pages

Our public website is an ordinary Shopify storefront and it carries advertising and analytics. They run on pages students use, including the page where a student sees their own progress and the page where they join a class. Signed-in teachers see no advertising.

As of the date at the top of this page the advertising is Raptive. The analytics are Microsoft Clarity, which records session replays, Google Analytics, Klaviyo for our mailing list, Ahrefs, and Shopify's own. The analytics run for every visitor across the site and are not switched off on student pages.

None of them is handed a student identifier. We do not pass a display name, a student id, or a session token to any of them, and we check the rendered pages to confirm it rather than taking it on trust. What they receive is that a page was viewed.

We are telling you this because your agreement will ask about targeted advertising and because saying otherwise would be false. If your district requires that no advertising or session replay run on pages students use while signed in, raise it with us before you sign rather than after.

Student work is kept while the class exists, because a gradebook that quietly drops last semester is not a gradebook. There is no automatic purge and we would rather say so than imply a schedule we do not run.
A teacher can delete a class at any time from their dashboard. That removes the class, its students, and all of their progress and attempts in one action, and it is not recoverable afterwards.

Deactivating a student is a different thing and it is deliberately not deletion. It removes them from the active roster and keeps their grade history, which is what a teacher usually wants at the end of a term. If you want the record gone, delete rather than deactivate, or ask us.

A teacher can already see, correct and delete everything we hold for their own class: the roster, every score, a student's name, and the class itself. For most requests the teacher is the fastest path and needs nothing from us.

For a formal request from a parent, a student or a district, write to us and we will action it. We will confirm in writing what was deleted and when. We do not require a particular form and we do not charge for it.
If your district needs a signed data privacy agreement, send us yours. We will sign an NDPA rather than insisting on our own terms.
Questions about this page, a deletion request, or an agreement to review: use the contact form on this site and say it is about student data so it gets routed properly.

This page describes how the product actually behaves, checked against the running system on the date shown, not how we intend it to behave. If you find something here that does not match what you observe, tell us and we will correct the page.
